proof_summary: At \(n=5319426\), the Sierpiński number \(K=59496778573193=a(n)+4\) lies strictly between the proposed consecutive pair.  Indeed, the exponent classes \(e\equiv0\pmod2,\ 3\pmod4,\ 1\pmod3,\ 1\pmod8,\ 5\pmod{48},\ 21\pmod{48},\ 13\pmod{16}\) cover all exponents and respectively force divisibility of \(K2^e+1\) by \(3,5,7,17,97,673,257\), proving that \(K\) is Sierpiński.
